data.title: NextEra Energy stock struggles: Oversold bounce or another leg lower?
data.description:
NextEra Energy (NEE) continued its downward trend this week, falling nearly 3% to around $85.08, as regulatory uncertainty surrounding its proposed merger with Dominion Energy (D) and concerns over capital-intensive growth weighed on sentiment.

The stock has gained just 5.93% year-to-date, underperforming the S&P 500's (SP500) 10.92% advance.

The proposed $67B merger with Dominion remains a significant overhang. Virginia regulators are scheduled to begin evidentiary hearings on November 17, ahead of a January 11, 2027, decision deadline.

Although the companies agreed to 114 of 117 staff-proposed conditions and pledged more than $2.25B in shareholder-funded bill credits and economic commitments, disagreements over a proposed six-year residential rate freeze have intensified opposition to the deal.

Technically, NextEra Energy has formed a bearish pattern of lower highs and lower lows throughout the week. The shares retreated from approximately $88 to a low near $84.45 before recovering modestly to around $85.07.

Repeated failed rebounds near $87 further reinforced the downward trend.

Momentum indicators also reflected the weakness. The 14-period RSI dropped below 20 during both major selloffs, signaling deeply oversold conditions, while the MACD moved below zero with widening negative histogram bars.

However, recent readings suggest an attempt at short-term stabilization. RSI has recovered to 53.38, above its 48.35 signal average, while MACD has crossed above its signal line, producing a slightly positive histogram.

The $86 resistance zone is the immediate level to watch. A sustained breakout above this range, supported by stronger volume, could signal improving momentum.

Failure to reclaim it may leave shares vulnerable to another test of the ~$84.45 weekly low. Meanwhile, investors will continue monitoring the Dominion merger proceedings for clarity on regulatory and financial risks.

data.title: York Space Systems downgraded at Jefferies, citing delayed path to positive EBITDA
data.description:
York Space Systems (YSS) plunged 11.6% in Friday's trading to a 52-week intraday low of $5.13 after posting a larger than expected Q3 loss while revenue slid 7% Y/Y, and the company wrote down $749.7M of goodwill as it cannot see the timing or size of contract awards past 2026.

In response to the disappointing Q3 report, Jefferies analyst Sheila Kahyaoglu cut York Space (YSS) from Hold from Buy with a $6 price target, slashed from $15, saying the results revealed a more elevated operating expense structure following recent acquisitions and limited new order intake, which suggest "a materially longer path to positive EBITDA, which now is not expected until 2028 at the earliest.

York Space (YSS) "has shifted from a near-term operating leverage/EBITDA inflection focus to a 'show-me' order conversion story with a meaningfully higher fixed cost base," which is "not just a one-quarter timing issue," as larger orders may come more in late 2027-28, Kahyaoglu said.

"We no longer see positive EBITDA until 2028 at the [earliest] and now believe revenues need to be greater than $600M for positive EBITDA... presenting further estimate risk if award timing doesn't materialize or subsidiary sales ramp more slowly," the analyst wrote.

data.title: Don't see lot of displacement from AI, but see less need to hire more: San Francisco Fed's Daly
data.description:
"You don't see a lot of displacement from AI yet, but you do see less need to hire additional people," said Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly.

"I think that's contributing to slow hiring, particularly hard on younger workers," she noted.

"You'll see that the unemployment rate for new college graduates has risen more and stayed higher," said Daly. "You can't put a single reason for that on a trend or pattern."

"It could really just come from if you're not hiring people, then the person you're not hiring is going to be predominantly a new college graduate or a new high school graduate."

Daly was speaking at a moderated discussion before the University of Nevada, Las Vegas Center for Business and Economic Research, or CBER, Forecast event.

On the question of why wage growth is not rising, she said when the labor market is stable, you don't see a lot of upward pressure on wages. 

"You know, employers are for whatever reasons, whether that's they're uncertain or they're just finding ways to be more efficient or they don't see their output growing as rapidly as it once was, or, importantly, they're trying to figure out what they can do with AI."

On being asked about the shrinking share of labor's output in the economy versus capital, Daly said the labor share of income is falling everywhere in the world and not just the U.S.

"What's driving it?"

"You really have to go to the falling price of capital. When the capital price falls relative to its historical level, businesses buy more capital," according to the Federal Open Market Committee's alternate voting member.

The second component of that equation is when real wages are falling, the real share of labor falls. 

What's really remarkable in many ways is that businesses across the U.S. are cautiously optimistic. They see opportunities for the future, according to Daly.

"Maybe the Fed will have to raise rates more than they expected, and so that will constrain growth and make it harder to manage the opportunities that they see," said the San Francisco Fed president.

data.title: Viking Therapeutics gains amid report of renewed takeover interest

data.title: The Fed should not raise 50 basis points in interest rates, says Goldman Sachs’s Robin Brooks
data.description:
Robin J. Brooks, former chief economist at the Institute of International Finance and chief FX strategist at Goldman Sachs, argued that

A 50-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike "won't and shouldn't happen" given the current economic uncertainty.

 According to Brooks, "another 50 or 100 basis points in hikes will do almost nothing to bring down inflation" because much of the recent price pressure stems from supply disruptions rather than overheating demand.

The strategist distinguished between two forces driving U.S. inflation: a series of supply shocks—including COVID in 2020, the oil price (CL1:COM), (CO1:COM) spike after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, reciprocal tariffs in 2025, and the war with Iran—and a potential rise in underlying inflation since the pandemic.

"Because there's long and variable lags in how supply shocks feed into inflation, we don't know where one shock ends and the next one begins," he said, making it difficult to determine what role supply disruptions play in current elevated readings.

Brooks contended that rate hikes are ineffective against supply-driven inflation, while the tightening required to address underlying inflation "is so big that it'd tip the economy into recession."

He characterized the anticipated hikes as "performative," explaining that "their purpose is to make it look like the Fed is doing its job."

The former Goldman Sachs strategist added that the current Fed "doesn't have the stomach" for the aggressive action that would genuinely cool underlying inflation.

Looking ahead, Brooks noted that "a 25-basis-point hike is all but inevitable in December," but emphasized that a larger move should not occur.

According to the strategist, it would be better for the Fed to "wait for the oil shock to pass and then see where underlying inflation settles."

"Better to go slow if you have to go at all,” he said.

data.title: Coca-Cola prints a new all-time high as the 'boring cash machine' rolls on
data.description:
Coca-Cola (KO) was up 1.7% in Friday afternoon trading and carved out a new all-time high of $99.28 along the way. The 10% push higher in Coca-Cola (KO) over the last few weeks has coincided with the unwinding of the AI trade and concerns over interest rate-sensitive stocks. 

Wall Street is still bullish on Coca-Cola (KO) despite the extended rally, while the Seeking Alpha Quant Rating is only at Hold due to valuation metrics that are well above historical averages and those of consumer staples peers.

Last month, Seeking Alpha analyst Elina Selianska called Coca-Cola (KO) the "boring cash machine" that beats bonds. She highlighted that even in the hardest economic crises, Coca-Cola (KO) manages to "calmly earn profit and generate free cash flow."  For long-term investors, Selianska thinks the best decision is treating the stock as an eternal rent-generating deposit.

data.title: Digi Power X targets $250M-$300M annualized revenue run rate by end of Q3 2027 as Columbiana Phase 1 billing nears
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Digi Power X Inc. (DGXX) Q3 2026

Management view

  • “Our third quarter results show that Digi Power X transformation into AI infrastructure company is beginning to take hold.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • The company reported a sharp sequential step-up in scale and mix, including revenue of $12.25 million, AI revenue of $5.66 million (46% of total), GPU rental bare metal through NeoCloudz of $2.46 million, and energy sales of $3.29 million, while stating “Legacy Bitcoin activities fell to approximately 27% of revenue from 63% a year ago. AI revenue more than offset that decline.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Profitability and balance sheet highlights were framed around non-GAAP improvement and liquidity, including “positive EBITDA of $6.5 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million” and “Cash and cash equivalents and digital currencies of $119.6 million,” alongside “No outstanding borrowings as of today.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • The core near-term execution catalyst was the Columbiana, Alabama AI campus timeline: “We expect to give our tenant access to the Phase 1 facility on December 15, 2026” with “Phase 1 billing expected to begin in January 2027,” while “targeting tenant access for Phase 2 in March 2027.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • The Cerebras colocation contract economics were presented as long-dated and expandable: “Phase 1 fees averaging approximately $40 million per year… or approximately $402 million in total,” and “Phase 2 will add approximately $58.5 million in annual fees… a total contract value to approximately $1.07 billion for both phases,” plus an expansion option “to approximately $2.5 billion.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Management highlighted a product shift up the stack with NeoCloudz: “NeoCloudz Token Factory is live,” adding, “The huge advantage of that are the margins. We see margins anywhere from 85% to 90%, actual margins.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • On financing, management said it had “received a commitment letter… for $200 million in debt financing syndicated by Goldman Sachs,” with closing “expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to definitive documentation and the satisfaction of various conditions.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • No CFO or separate finance executive remarks were included in this transcript.

Outlook

  • “We expect to reach an annualized revenue run rate of approximately $250 million to $300 million or approximately $21 million to $25 million per month by the end of third quarter 2027, subject to adequate financing, market conditions and various other conditions.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • Management attributed approximately $143 million of the targeted run rate to “current operation and the Columbiana tenant agreement,” with the remainder expected from “additional AI colocation and GPU capacity currently in development and in customer negotiations.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Capital intensity was guided explicitly: “We expect 2027 CapEx of approximately $350 million,” intended to be funded “principally through customer deposits and prepayment and contract debt financing, including the proposed $200 million facility together with cash on hand,” and described as “designed to minimize shareholder dilution.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Relative to Q2, management’s Columbiana timeline language stayed centered on Phase 1 in December 2026 and Phase 2 by end of Q1 2027/March 2027, but Q3 added specific billing start months (January 2027 for Phase 1; April 2027 referenced later for Phase 2). (Chairman & CEO Amar)

Financial results

  • The company reported “revenue went up 85% to $12.25 million from the second quarter of 2026,” and said “Positive net income of $1 million materially supported by digital currency and warrant valuation gains.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • Liquidity and investment levels were highlighted as of September 30, 2026, including “Working capital of $103 million,” “Digital currency holding of $24.5 million,” and “net fixed assets of $145.6 million… reflecting infrastructure investment primarily at the Columbiana, Alabama facility.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Management also provided an intra-quarter update: “Balance sheet and liquidity as of today, November 13. The company's cash, cash equivalents is approximately a little bit above $100 million cash,” and stated “$168 million year-to-date capital expenditure deployed towards GPU equipment and data center build-out at the Columbiana, Alabama facility.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Cost discipline was referenced late in the call: “we lowered our SG&A expenses 30% from Q2 to Q3.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

Q&A

  • Operator: what do Q3 results demonstrate about the AI transformation? Chairman & CEO Amar: “we went from no cash, little assets, a Bitcoin dying business to cash… and AI revenues that represents almost half of our total revenue.”

  • Operator: how much revenue is recurring or contracted? Chairman & CEO Amar: “Phase 1 represents approximately $402 million in contractual fees, increasing to approximately $1.07 billion with Phase 2,” while adding NeoCloudz contract duration “vary anywhere from 2 to 5 years.”

  • Operator: what does the December 15 milestone represent? Chairman & CEO Amar: “tenants will have access to the data hall… after the commissioning, we can start billing.”

  • Operator: where does the proposed $200 million financing stand? Chairman & CEO Amar: “We are pretty close to close the financing… definitely in Q4 '26,” and said the company “managed to be in single-digit interest.”

  • Operator: how will the $350 million 2027 capital plan be funded while minimizing dilution? Chairman & CEO Amar: “Now they're willing to give you 30% and sometimes up to 50%… And sometimes… up to 70%,” citing larger customer deposits after recent market weakness.

  • Operator: can operations generate sustained positive cash flow? Chairman & CEO Amar: “We generated $4.7 million of positive cash flow in Q3, through, with the help of a $12 million nonrefundable tenant infrastructure contribution.”

  • Operator: what drove NeoCloudz’ growth and are margins sustainable? Chairman & CEO Amar discussed pricing and constraints, stating, “Bare metal today… we can book short-term B300 at $775 per hour,” and “If we do tokens, it's $15 to $20 per hour equivalent per token.”

  • Operator: how do Cerebras 3Q results impact Digi Power? Chairman & CEO Amar: “Their results yesterday showed that they are doing great,” and said, “we are very confident that our relationship with Cerebras has detonated our credibility.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was not directly observable because the Q&A questions were presented by the Operator rather than named analysts; questions repeatedly pressed on execution milestones, contracted revenue, financing timing, dilution control, and cash flow durability.

  • Management sentiment was positive and emphatic in both prepared remarks and Q&A, using confidence language such as “We don't see any issues,” “we are very confident,” and “It's very simple. It's purely execution.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • Versus the prior quarter, management’s tone shifted from establishing eligibility for debt financing to asserting near-term closings and delivery specifics, including “we are pretty close to close the financing” and detailed commissioning/billing dates. (Chairman & CEO Amar)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q3 emphasized a sharper pivot toward AI monetization, stating AI revenue was $5.66 million and “representing now 46% of total revenue,” while Q2 described “GPU revenue recognized for $1.1 million, representing the company's first GPU bare-metal rental.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • Liquidity language tightened from Q2’s “cash and cash equivalents of $142.4 million” (as of June 30) and “approximately $150 million today” (at that time) to Q3’s “approximately a little bit above $100 million cash” (as of November 13), alongside higher year-to-date CapEx ($110 million in Q2 vs. $168 million in Q3). (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Financing discussion evolved from Q2 “advanced debt financing discussions” to Q3’s announced “commitment letter… for $200 million,” with closing targeted in Q4 2026. (Chairman & CEO Amar)

Risks and concerns

  • Financing remained conditional: the $200 million facility was described as subject to “definitive documentation” and “due diligence.” (Chairman & CEO Michel Amar)

  • Management tied growth targets to multiple dependencies, stating the $250 million to $300 million run-rate goal was “subject to adequate financing, market conditions and various other conditions.” (Chairman & CEO Amar)

  • Execution and timing risk was implicitly acknowledged through milestone focus, with management repeatedly pointing investors to Phase 1 access/commissioning, billing start, and Phase 2 access/billing as the near-term scorecard. (Chairman & CEO Amar)

Final takeaway

Management framed Q3 as evidence that Digi Power X’s shift away from legacy Bitcoin toward AI infrastructure and GPU services is translating into faster growth and a higher AI mix ahead of Columbiana colocation billing beginning in January 2027. The company highlighted long-term contracted economics with Cerebras, launched the NeoCloudz Token Factory with stated 85% to 90% margins, and reiterated a financing-and-customer-deposit funding approach aimed at limiting dilution while targeting a $250 million to $300 million annualized revenue run rate by end of Q3 2027.
